parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a federal document/entry regime (X markers halted, M/F-only processing, a consular cable ordering refusal where records cast doubt on sex, with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility considered) on a division that bans facility use matching gender identity in state buildings, bars marker changes, and denies public-funded gender-affirming care to adults. Custody carries documented severity: men's-ward placement, federal conversion-therapy policy, and abuse in immigration detention. No criminalisation of trans identity as such exists; emergency care is exempt, private care remains, national hate-crime protection and functioning courts operate, and several orders are enjoined. Exposures are universal but exclusionary rather than custodial by default.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and to weigh fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X markers ended; passports blocked/confused; travellers stranded; multiple foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, waivers exist, never automatic; policy is under active litigation; legal-aid FAQ tracks rules; existing X passports valid to expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Division closure of marker changes raises the odds a visitor's presentation diverges from any matching document, feeding the federal refusal trigger.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward after a restroom trespass arrest in a neighbouring division; federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (hair, hormones, psychiatric drugs) from 2026; trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release was granted; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts function and several federal orders are enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document mismatch can escalate into immigration custody, where documented abuse applies to trans detainees.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division bans facility use per gender identity in K-12 (2022, 2025) and a 2023 executive order applies birth-sex definitions to all state-owned facilities (bathrooms, shelters, incarceration); federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; trespass is criminal in 4 states nationally with one documented arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart after request; enumerated exemptions include emergencies; 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a restroom in a state capitol, state park or public university in this division meets both the division order and the federal facility rule.

care_services.exposure: SB 904 (signed 14 May 2026, immediate) bars public funds, Medicaid and state facilities for gender-affirming care for minors and adults; intentional employee violations are a misdemeanour; care reduced to privately owned facilities paid privately.
care_services.protection: Emergency treatment to prevent death or major impairment is exempt; mental-health, intersex and complication care exempt; private providers remain available.
care_services.interaction: Federal October 2025 proposed rules would additionally bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18s, compounding the division ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names ideology 'hostile to the country, radically pro-transgender' for identification and neutralisation; Dec 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; 66% poll support for birth-sex markers on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward memo never uses the phrase as a criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; national employment and hate-crime protections persist.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Heightened framing raises discovery and scrutiny probability rather than creating a standalone offence against visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; division bans minor gender-affirming care and school facilities congruent with identity; a trans minor using school or state facilities risks trespass exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: SB 904 states patients face no penalties; care exemptions cover mental health and emergencies; national workplace protections cover accompanying adults.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor moves between a federal criminal-referral posture and division facility/care bans at schools and public venues.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime coverage of gender identity and no state discrimination statute; only one city with full protections; 2018 death threats against a 12-year-old student; a student died after a school bathroom beating (2024).
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute adds penalties for gender-identity-motivated crime; no documented killing or state violence against a visitor in this division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin local recourse means federal prosecution is the realistic channel if bias violence occurs.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: HB 1225 signature status unresolved; division's July 2026 risk grade unstated; driver's licence marker status unknown; litigation makes exposure vary by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple active suits, a legal-aid FAQ, courts enjoining several federal orders, and national hate-crime prosecution provide real if uneven recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertain paper status does not cancel documented operative rules already in force (facility order, SB 904, consular cable).

anchor_checks.comparison: Ostravia imposes universal lodging reporting with eviction and fund freezes but no custody. This jurisdiction has no documented hotel-reporting duty, yet its entry-refusal policy, birth-sex custody placement and documented immigration-custody abuse are more severe on the custody axis, so the rating sits slightly below this anchor.

Vesskar shows routine document/facility exposure, detention, care denial, scarce legal aid and inconsistent enforcement. Very close: here the entry rule is a formal written cable rather than discretionary checks, and division custody/facility rules are explicit, but federal courts, litigation and the national hate-crime statute supply somewhat stronger recourse.

Marisol Union's ward-by-document rule with ombuds and ethics remedies is materially softer: administrative delay and misplacement rather than entry refusal, criminal trespass exposure for facility use, and a public-facility care ban. This dossier's documented exposures outweigh it, so it rates clearly lower than 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: federal document and consular rules determine whether entry is granted at all, while the division supplies the facilities, care and custody layer. Document mismatch raises discovery probability; the cable converts discovery into refusal or possible fraud findings, with only contested litigation and advisory help as recourse. Inside the division, state-building facilities are governed by a birth-sex order backed by a trespass offence already tested by arrest elsewhere, and public-facility adult care is barred with an emergency carve-out. Detention, if triggered, places the traveller by birth sex and can reach federal or immigration custody where abuse is documented. Counterbalancing: no offence punishes trans identity itself, private care and lodging remain, national hate-crime and employment protections operate, and courts are actively enjoining the harshest measures.
